# TIMP (Travel in my pocket): how to write a trip file

> For AI assistants asked to make or change a trip for TIMP, a web app (https://frafal.github.io/TIMP/)
> that shows a day-by-day travel guide on a phone, offline. A trip is ONE JSON file that
> says what the trip is: days, stops, where to sleep, what to remember. Never how it
> looks: the app picks colours, draws maps and chooses icons. The app refuses the whole
> file if one rule is broken, so follow the format below exactly and invent no fields.
> This page is complete: the format, the guide and a full example are all here. Do not
> look for other files.
> The format as a JSON Schema: https://frafal.github.io/TIMP/trip.schema.json

**Version 4.2.1.** TIMP is under active development and this page changes with it.
Remember this version. Before you change a trip later in the conversation, or when a
message from the app names a newer TIMP version, open this page again: if its version
is newer, read "What's new" and use it. If you cannot open it, ask the traveller for
the message the app copies (Trips → Have an AI assistant change this trip): it always
carries the current format.

## When TIMP is linked to this chat

If you have TIMP's tools (`list_trips`, `get_trip`, `change_trip`…), the traveller
linked their TIMP account to this chat: use the tools, not files. They read and change
the trips on the account directly, and say how. Without them, a traveller with a TIMP
account can link you: in TIMP, You → Linked chats → Link a chat.

## What's new

Only what a trip file, or a list of changes, can say differently. Files written for an
older version still load.

- **3.26**: `basedOn` on the trip, written by the app on a copy of a published trip
  (`url`, `title`, `by`). Optional.
- **3.9**: changes say the version they were written for: `from`, from the outline.
- **3.8**: a `cost` is what the traveller pays, their share of what is split; in 3.7
  it was the total for everyone. Private expenses: `private`, with its `expenses` (a
  private one can name the `stop` where it was paid) and `owner`, outside versions and
  merges. Changes reach them with `"private": true`.

## The format, in short

```text
TIMP trip file, format "travel-in-my-pocket/2". Answer with ONE JSON object in one code block: double quotes, no comments, no trailing commas. Use only these fields; invent none.

trip:
  format (required): "travel-in-my-pocket/2"
  title (required): text. The name of the trip.
  days (required): list of day. One entry per date, in date order.
  lang: en|it. Language of the app while this trip is open. Without it, the phone's.
  timezone: an IANA time zone such as "Europe/Rome". Time zone of the destination: decides which day is today.
  info: list of section. Sections of the Info page: numbers, words, transport.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of every cost without its own.
  expenses: list of expense. Money spent outside the stops: flights, hotels, passes.
  private: private. The traveller's own spending, not shared.
day:
  date (required): a real date as "YYYY-MM-DD". The date.
  city: text. Where the day is spent: a city or an area.
  title: text. What the day is about, in a few words.
  stay: text or stay. Where the night is spent: a name, or an object with name, address and note.
  notes: list of text. Things to remember that day, shown at the top.
  stops: list of stop. The stops, in order. A day has `stops` or `plans`.
  plans: list of plan. Alternative plans for the day, each with its own stops.
plan:
  name (required): text. The name of the plan, shown on its button.
  stops (required): list of stop. The stops of this plan, in order.
  chosen: true. On the plan the day goes with. None: the first.
stop:
  title (required): text. The name of the place or of the activity.
  local: text. The name in the local script, as on the sign ("一蘭 渋谷店"): to show staff, and to search it.
  time: "HH:MM" or sunrise|morning|midday|afternoon|sunset|evening|night. When: a clock time, or a part of the day (sunrise and sunset at their real time where the day is). For all day, no time.
  type: sight|museum|food|park|view|shop|walk|hotel. What kind of place it is; it gives the stop its icon and pin.
  travel: metro|bus|train|plane|boat. How you get there from the stop before.
  text: text. What to know: what to see, what to order, tickets. **bold** is allowed.
  tag: text. A short label shown on the stop, like "Booked 19:30" or "Optional".
  booking: required|advised|booked. "required": no entry without it (the app warns); "advised": better booked; "booked": done.
  cost: number, 0 or more. What the traveller pays. 0: free.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of `cost`, if not the trip's.
  closed: list of "mon" to "sun", or a date as "YYYY-MM-DD". Days of the week and dates the place is closed: the app warns on them.
  address: text. As you would search it in Google Maps: a street address, or name and town.
  lat: number from -90 to 90. Latitude, with `lng`: the pin on the map.
  lng: number from -180 to 180. Longitude, with `lat`.
  link: an https:// address. A Google Maps link to the exact place.
  choice: text. Options for one moment: stops of a day with the same choice ("Lunch"), 2 to 4.
  chosen: true. On the option the day goes to. None: to choose.
expense:
  title (required): text. What it was: "Flights", "Hotel, 3 nights".
  cost (required): number, 0 or more. What the traveller pays.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of `cost`, if not the trip's.
  date: a real date as "YYYY-MM-DD". When it was paid: the day of its rate. Without it, the trip's first day.
private:
  expenses (required): list of expense. Shopping, a meal alone.
stay:
  name (required): text. The name of the hotel or flat.
  address: text. Its address.
  note: text. Check-in, booking, how to get in.
section:
  title (required): text. The title of the section.
  items (required): list of item. Its lines.
item:
  label (required): text. What the line is about.
  text (required): text. The line itself. Phone numbers become a link to call.

Rules: days in date order, one per date. A day has stops or plans (two or more), never both. Plans only when the whole day changes; for one meal, a choice. lat and lng go together. No colours, icons, ids or versions: the app adds them. Do not invent bookings, hotels or prices. A cost is what the traveller pays: their share if split. Give lat/lng only for places you are sure about; otherwise an address.

Example:
{"format":"travel-in-my-pocket/2","title":"Rome in three days","lang":"en","days":[{"date":"2027-04-10","city":"Rome","title":"The ancient city","stay":{"name":"Hotel Example","address":"Via Cavour 1, Rome"},"notes":["Colosseum tickets booked for 9:00"],"stops":[{"time":"09:00","title":"Colosseum","type":"sight","text":"Enter from the Via Sacra side.","address":"Piazza del Colosseo, Rome","lat":41.8902,"lng":12.4922},{"time":"midday","title":"Lunch in Monti","type":"food","travel":"metro"}]}],"info":[{"title":"In case of need","items":[{"label":"Emergency","text":"112"}]}]}
```

## Changing a trip that already exists

When the traveller gives you an outline of their trip (lines like
`[colosseum] 09:00 Colosseum (sight)`), do not write the whole file again: answer
with the changes only.

```text
To change an existing trip, answer with ONE JSON object in one code block, format "travel-in-my-pocket/changes", listing only what changes:

{"format": "travel-in-my-pocket/changes", "trip": "<the trip id>", "from": "<the version in the outline>", "changes": [ … ]}

"from" lets the app apply the changes to the trip as you saw it, and join them with what changed on the phone since.

Each change is one of:
  {"add": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": {…}}}             a new stop (fields: title, local, time, type, travel, text, tag, booking, cost, currency, closed, address, lat, lng, link, choice, chosen); it goes in time order
  {"update": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": "<id>", "set": {…}}}  changed fields of a stop; null removes a field
  {"update": {"day": …, "stop": "<id>", "to": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}}  moves the stop to another day (set may go with it)
  {"remove": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": "<id>"}}
  {"setDay": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "set": {…}}}             a day's city, title, stay or notes ("notes": the whole list, as it should be)
  {"addDay": {…a whole day, as in a trip file…}}
  {"removeDay": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}
  {"addPlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": {"name": "…", "stops": [{…}, …]}, "first": "…"}}  an alternative plan for the day (a rainy day, a lazy morning); the traveller picks one. On a day without plans, "first" names the plan made of the stops it has now
  {"setPlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": "<plan id>", "set": {"name": "…"}}}  renames a plan
  {"removePlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": "<plan id>"}}  with one plan left, the day has plain stops again
  {"setTrip": {"set": {…}}}  the trip's title, lang, timezone, info, currency, private
  {"addExpense": {"expense": {"title": "…", "cost": 0, "currency": "EUR", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}}  money spent outside the stops (flights, hotels)
  {"setExpense": {"expense": "<id>", "set": {…}}}  /  {"removeExpense": {"expense": "<id>"}}
  "private": true next to "expense", in these three: the traveller's private expenses (shopping, a meal alone), not shared with the trip. A private one paid at a stop has "stop": "<stop id>" and that day as "date"

Options for one moment (a meal): stops with the same "choice" ("Lunch"), 2 to 4; "chosen": true on the one the day goes to (the others lose it). Plans only when the whole day changes.

On days with plans, add "plan": "<plan id>" next to "day". Use the ids in square brackets from the outline, copied exactly; new stops have none. Give lat and lng for new places when you know them. A cost is what the traveller pays (their share of what is split), in the trip's currency unless the stop says another; write only prices you know.
```

## How the traveller loads it

They copy your answer and tap Paste in the app (or save it as a .json file and load
it). If the app refuses it, it lists each problem with its position, like
`days[0].stops[2].title: is required`, and a button copies that list to send back to
you. Fix every problem and send your answer again.

---

# Creating a trip file

How to turn a trip plan into a file for TIMP (Travel in my pocket). This guide is for whoever
writes the file: a person, or an AI assistant working for one. It says how to write a
*good* file; the list of fields and what is valid is in the format reference (further down this page).

The reader of the result is someone standing in a street abroad with a phone in one
hand, often without a connection. Everything in the file should help that person
decide what to do next.

## What you produce

One JSON file in the format `travel-in-my-pocket/2`. It says what the trip is: days,
stops, stays, things to remember. Never how it looks: the app picks colours, draws the
maps and chooses the icons from the content.

A trip file contains hotels and dates. Treat it as private: give it to the traveller and
nobody else, and never publish it.

## 1. Collect the trip

You need: the dates, the places, where the travellers sleep each night, and what they
do each day. Read everything you were given before asking anything. Then ask only for
what is missing and changes the result: travel dates, hotel names, fixed bookings
(flights, trains, timed tickets).

Do not invent bookings, hotels, flight times or reservations. If something is not
decided, leave it out or present it as an option (`"tag": "Optional"`, a line in
`notes`, or alternative `plans`).

If there is only a rough idea ("5 days in Lisbon"), agree on a programme first and
write the file afterwards. A file is a bad place to negotiate an itinerary.

## 2. Write the days

One entry per date, from the arrival day to the departure day, in date order.

- `city`: where the day is spent ("Lisbon", "Sintra"). Days in the same city share a
  colour, and a change of city shows on the day ("Lisbon → Porto"). Write it the same
  way every day.
- `title`: what the day is about, in a few words ("Baixa and Alfama on foot").
- `stay`: where the night is spent. The full object (`name`, `address`, `note` with
  check-in and booking details) on every night in that hotel; a plain name for nights
  that are not a hotel ("Night train").
- `notes`: only what would spoil the day if forgotten, and the alternative. "The last
  ferry back leaves at 17:30." "If it rains, swap with day 4." Zero to three per day.
- `stops`: in the order they happen. Include the practical ones too: arrival,
  check-in, the train to the next city, the way back to the hotel.
- `plans` instead of `stops` only when the travellers will choose on the spot between
  two or three different days (a rainy day, a lazy one). Each plan has a `name` and its
  `stops`.
- For options at one moment (three places for lunch, one museum or another), not plans:
  two to four stops with the same `choice` (`"Lunch"`), side by side in the day, and
  `"chosen": true` on the one you suggest, or on none to leave it to the travellers.

## 3. Write the stops

- `time`: a clock time when it matters ("09:30"), a part of the day when it does not:
  `sunrise`, `morning`, `midday`, `afternoon`, `sunset`, `evening`, `night`, in English
  whatever the trip's language. Leave it out for all day.
- `title`: the name of the place as written on maps and signs.
- `local`: the same name in the local script, as on the sign ("一蘭 渋谷店", "명동교자"),
  wherever the country does not write in the Latin alphabet. Leave it out otherwise.
- `type`: what kind of place it is. One of `sight` (monuments, churches, squares),
  `museum`, `food` (restaurants, cafés, markets to eat at), `park` (parks, gardens,
  beaches), `view` (viewpoints), `shop`, `walk` (a stroll through a quarter), `hotel`.
  Leave it out for anything else (a station, a journey).
- `travel`: how the travellers reach this stop, when it is by `metro`, `bus`, `train`,
  `plane` or `boat`. Set it every time the description says so ("bus 7 from the
  station"). Leave it out for walking and anything else. A journey that is a stop of
  its own ("Train to Kyoto", "Flight to Rome") gets `travel` and no position.
- `text`: one to three sentences, in this order of usefulness: how to get there from
  the previous stop (line, direction, minutes), price and opening hours, what to look
  at, one tip. The app shows the first two lines until the traveller taps, so put what
  matters most first. Write in the travellers' language and tone.
- `tag`: what to know at a glance, in the trip's language: "Ticket needed",
  "Booked 19:30 · 2 people", "Cash only", "Optional".
- `booking`: `required` when there is no way in without booking, `advised` when going
  without is a gamble, `booked` only when the traveller says it is done. Never write
  `booked` on your own. Museums and shows can need it too.
- `closed`: the regular closing days ("mon") and closures on the dates of the trip
  ("2027-05-03"), when you know them. The app warns if the stop falls on one.
- `address`: where it is, as someone would type it into Google Maps: a street address,
  or the name and the town ("Pantheon, Rome"). It drives the Map and Directions links.
- `lat`, `lng`: the position, four decimal places. Look it up on a map or on the web
  whenever you can. From memory, give it only for places you are sure about (major
  landmarks, main stations). For a small restaurant you cannot verify, leave the
  position out and write a good `address`: the stop still gets working links.
- `link`: a Google Maps link to the exact place, when the traveller gave you one.
- No position for stops that are not a place: a train ride, "free afternoon".

Tell the traveller which positions were not verified.

### Places to eat

Meals are what travellers remember, and what goes wrong most easily: a closed door, a
two-hour queue, a counter that only takes bookings. For every place to eat:

- `type`: `food`, and `local` wherever the sign is not in the Latin alphabet. In Japan
  many places have a sign only in Japanese; the app also searches the reviews by it.
- `booking` and `closed` as above. Many restaurants in Japan close one fixed day a
  week, and some on irregular days: then write "check the closing days" in `text`.
- `text`: what to order, how it works (queue, ticket machine at the door, counter
  seats, cash only), the price per person, then one tip.
- No links to review sites (Tabelog, Yelp, TheFork, Tripadvisor): their addresses carry
  numbers you cannot know. The app links each place to the reviews used in that
  country by itself.
- For a meal that matters (a famous place, a long queue), add a fallback nearby: a
  second food stop with the tag "Alternative".

Tell the traveller which closing days and booking rules were not verified.

### Costs

The app adds up what the trip costs the traveller who holds it, at the exchange rate of
each day. Every amount is **what that traveller pays**: their own share of what is split
with others. You know from the conversation who shares what; the app does not need to
know how many people travel. Give it what you know, and nothing you do not:

- `currency` on the trip: the money of the destination (`"JPY"` in Japan).
- `cost` on a stop, as a number: what the traveller pays there. A museum ticket at
  ¥1,200 is `1200`, whoever comes along; a dinner for two at ¥12,000 split in half is
  `6000`. Only prices you know: tickets, trains, a booked menu. A free sight is `0`; a
  price you are not sure of stays out, or goes in `text` as something to check.
- `currency` on a stop only when it is paid in another money (a ticket bought from home).
- `expenses` for what is paid outside the stops, often before leaving: flights,
  hotels, rail passes, insurance, each with `title`, `cost` and the `date` it was paid.
  A double room for two at €200 a night is `100` a night for the traveller. Only the
  ones the traveller told you about.
- `private` for what the traveller spends only for themselves and does not want in the
  shared trip: shopping, a meal alone. `{"expenses": [...]}`, written like the trip's
  expenses. Only when the traveller asks for it. In a file the app saved, keep
  `private.owner` exactly as it is; never write one yourself.

## 4. Facts that go out of date

Prices, opening hours, closing days, timetables and seasonal closures change.
Verify them when you can. When you cannot, either leave the detail out or word it as
something to check ("check the timetable on the day"), and tell the traveller which
facts were not verified. Never state an unverified price or time as certain.

## 5. The Info page

Keep it to what someone needs in a hurry: emergency numbers, how to pay and get cash,
how luggage moves between hotels, booking codes, five or six phrases in the local
language. Each section has a `title` and `items` of `label` and `text`; a text that is
only a phone number can be tapped to call. The stays are listed there by the app.

## 6. Check the file

**Without Node:** load the file in the app (or paste it: Trips → Paste a trip). It
runs the same checks and lists every problem with its position in the file, for
example `days[2].stops[0].lat: must be a number between -90 and 90`. Fix them and load
it again. When an assistant wrote the file, "Copy for the assistant" copies the list
with a request to fix it, ready to paste into the chat. Then open the map of each day
and look for a pin in the wrong place.

## 7. Hand it over

Tell the travellers, briefly:

1. Send the file to each phone (chat, AirDrop, Drive), or the JSON to copy.
2. Open the app **from its Home Screen icon** and choose "Load a trip file", or
   "Paste a trip". On an iPhone, loading it in Safari instead puts it in a different
   storage.
3. Open the app once with a connection before leaving.
4. What could not be verified: positions, prices, hours.

## Updating a file later

**An AI assistant in a chat:** the traveller sends an outline of the trip (from Trips →
Have an AI assistant change this trip). Answer with the changes only, in the format
`travel-in-my-pocket/changes` described in the format reference: never the whole file
again. Put the version named at the top of the outline in `from`.

**With the whole file:**

- Start from the latest file: travellers change trips in the app too, and save them
  from Trips → Save the file. An older copy loses nothing, because the app merges, but
  starting from the latest one avoids surprises.
- Keep the trip `id` and the `version` block exactly as they are, if the file has
  them: the app then updates the trip, keeps what was ticked, and makes a new version.
  Never write or change `version` yourself.
- Keep the `id` of every stop that still exists, even if it is renamed or moved. A new
  stop has no `id`; one copied from another stop leaves the copy's out.
- Keep `private` and its `owner` as they are, unless the traveller asked to change
  their private expenses.
- Change only what was asked. Do not rewrite texts nobody mentioned.
- Check the file again.

## The Google Maps key

Optional. Without it the interactive map uses OpenStreetMap. If the traveller has a
key and wants Google Maps, add `"googleMapsKey": "..."` at the top level.

- Only use a key the traveller gives you. Never invent one, never reuse one from
  another file.
- The key must be restricted to the app's address and to the Maps JavaScript API, with
  a daily quota. Google Maps explains how.
- A file with a key must not be published.

## Mistakes to avoid

- `"name"` for a stop: it is `"title"`. And `"format": "travel-in-my-pocket/2"` first.
- Positions swapped (`lat` is north-south, between -90 and 90).
- Two entries for the same date. Use `plans` for alternative days, `choice` for options
  at one moment.
- A day with both `stops` and `plans`, or with neither.
- Colours, icons or map settings: the file has none.
- Long paragraphs in `text`. The traveller reads this standing up.
- Links to review or booking pages you did not get from the traveller.
- Prices you guessed, or the total for everyone in `cost`: it is the traveller's share.
- Comments or trailing commas in the JSON.
- HTML in the texts. Only `**bold**` is formatting; everything else is shown as written.


---

# A complete example

```json
{"format": "travel-in-my-pocket/2", "title": "Lisbon in my pocket (example)", "lang": "en", "timezone": "Europe/Lisbon", "currency": "EUR", "expenses": [{"title":"Flights to Lisbon and back (invented)","date":"2026-10-05","cost":280},{"title":"Casa do Exemplo, 3 nights (invented)","date":"2026-11-02","cost":390}], "private": {"expenses":[{"title":"Azulejo tiles to take home (invented)","date":"2027-05-15","cost":24},{"title":"Port wine, a bottle for home (invented)","date":"2027-05-17","cost":18}]},
 "days": [
   {"date": "2027-05-14", "city": "Lisboa", "title": "Baixa and Alfama on foot", "stay": {"name":"Casa do Exemplo (invented)","address":"Baixa, Lisboa","note":"This hotel does not exist: it shows where the check-in notes go. **Bold** works here too."}, "notes": ["This is an invented trip, here to show what the app does. Times and descriptions are examples: check everything before a real visit.","If it rains: swap this day with the next one. **Belém** has more places indoors."],
    "stops": [
      {"time":"10:00","title":"Praça do Comércio","type":"sight","text":"Start at the big square on the river, then walk under the arch into Rua Augusta.","address":"Praça do Comércio Lisboa","lat":38.7075,"lng":-9.1364},
      {"time":"11:00","title":"Lisbon Cathedral","type":"sight","text":"Ten minutes uphill. The tram line passes right in front of the door.","cost":10,"address":"Sé de Lisboa","lat":38.7098,"lng":-9.1326},
      {"time":"11:45","title":"Miradouro de Santa Luzia","type":"view","text":"A terrace over the roofs of Alfama. A good place for a break.","address":"Miradouro de Santa Luzia","lat":38.7117,"lng":-9.1303},
      {"time":"12:30","title":"Castelo de São Jorge","type":"sight","text":"The castle on top of the hill. Tickets are sold at the gate.","tag":"Ticket needed","cost":30,"address":"Castelo de São Jorge","lat":38.7139,"lng":-9.1335,"link":"https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Castelo+de+S%C3%A3o+Jorge+Lisboa"},
      {"time":"14:00","title":"Lunch in Alfama","type":"food","text":"No coordinates on this stop: it has no pin on the map, and that is fine.","cost":38},
      {"time":"Evening","title":"Miradouro da Senhora do Monte","type":"view","text":"The highest viewpoint in the centre, best at sunset.","tag":"Optional","address":"Miradouro da Senhora do Monte","lat":38.7191,"lng":-9.1327}
    ]},
   {"date": "2027-05-15", "city": "Lisboa", "title": "Belém and the river", "stay": {"name":"Casa do Exemplo (invented)","address":"Baixa, Lisboa","note":"This hotel does not exist: it shows where the check-in notes go. **Bold** works here too."},
    "stops": [
      {"time":"09:30","title":"Mosteiro dos Jerónimos","type":"museum","text":"Go early: the queue grows during the morning.","tag":"Ticket needed","cost":36,"address":"Mosteiro dos Jerónimos","lat":38.6979,"lng":-9.2068},
      {"time":"11:00","title":"Pastéis de Belém","type":"food","text":"The custard tarts, still warm. The queue for take-away moves fast.","cost":6.4,"address":"Pastéis de Belém","lat":38.6975,"lng":-9.2032},
      {"time":"12:00","title":"Torre de Belém","type":"sight","text":"A walk along the river to the tower.","address":"Torre de Belém","lat":38.6916,"lng":-9.216},
      {"time":"14:30","title":"MAAT","type":"museum","text":"You can walk on the roof of the museum for free.","cost":22,"address":"MAAT Lisboa","lat":38.6959,"lng":-9.1937},
      {"time":"16:30","title":"LX Factory","type":"shop","text":"Shops and cafés in an old factory, under the bridge.","address":"LX Factory Lisboa","lat":38.7034,"lng":-9.1789},
      {"time":"18:00","title":"Cais do Sodré","travel":"train","text":"Back towards the centre on the Cascais line from Alcântara-Mar, a few minutes.","address":"Cais do Sodré station","lat":38.7056,"lng":-9.1446},
      {"time":"18:30","title":"Dinner in Cacilhas","type":"food","travel":"boat","text":"The ferry crosses the river in about ten minutes. Fish restaurants along the quay, and the city lit up across the water.","booking":"advised","cost":54,"address":"Cacilhas ferry terminal","lat":38.6873,"lng":-9.1475}
    ]},
   {"date": "2027-05-16", "city": "Sintra", "title": "A day out of town", "stay": {"name":"Casa do Exemplo (invented)","address":"Baixa, Lisboa","note":"This hotel does not exist: it shows where the check-in notes go. **Bold** works here too."}, "notes": ["A day with two alternative plans: pick one with the buttons below. The app remembers the choice."],
```
